text:
miriam: Quick results from the bring-up sweep for llama2-13b-int8 across h100/a100 in us-east/us-west/eu-west. Wanted to capture routing vs local-pop impact on p50/p95 and a quick capacity ballpark.

kevin: awesome — TL;DR numbers?

miriam: TL;DR: local-pop routing keeps p95 reasonable (roughly 1.5-2x p50), cross-pop routing (requests leaving local edge to us-east) increases p95 by ~2-4x depending on region/hardware. Throughput delta h100 vs a100 ~1.5-1.7x for int8 kernels.

anika: can you paste the slices?

miriam: paste below — single-generation 512-token context, batching tuned for 32/48 tokens avg, continuous batching on. All tests run w/ same quantized weights + kernel selection: fused_attention_v2 when available, fallback to generic_nhwc.

miriam: h100 (local pop) us-east: p50 62ms, p95 125ms, throughput ~18 req/s
miriam: a100 (local pop) us-east: p50 98ms, p95 240ms, throughput ~11 req/s

miriam: h100 eu-west local-pop: p50 78ms, p95 160ms, throughput ~15 req/s
miriam: h100 eu-west routed->us-east (edge routing forced remote): p50 210ms, p95 420ms, throughput ~6 req/s

miriam: a100 us-west routed->us-east: p50 270ms, p95 510ms, throughput ~4.5 req/s

raj: ouch — p95 blowups when crossing pops are expected but those numbers are big. what's causing the 2x-4x? extra network + extra proxy hops + cold proxy connections?

miriam: yup layered effect: extra hop latency + requeue/backpressure into remote-serving pool + slight KV cache miss when remote model variant has different cache warming. Also discovered that fused_attention_v2 kernel has better warmup behavior on h100; when fallback_nhwc used (a100 quant path) p95 tail suffers more.

anika: any config snippet for the routing policy you used?

miriam: added this ephemeral policy for the sweep:

```
route_policy:
  prefer: local_pop
  fallback: remote_same_model
  max_remote_hop_ms: 120
  allow_cross_region: true
```

miriam: when we flip prefer->us-east for eu-west requests, p95 jumps to the routed numbers above. when prefer: local_pop is enforced, p95 for eu-west/h100 was 160ms not 420ms.

kevin: quality / quant regressions? any eval diffs from fp16 baseline?

miriam: int8 quant (per-channel asymmetric) gave ~1.6x throughput on h100 across our harness. Eval set (SFT prompts + 1k held-out) shows ~0.4% absolute drop in Rouge-like score and a small 0.7% perplexity increase — within acceptable band for many infra-backed use cases but flagging for product teams. We'll surface failing prompts in the eval dashboard.

raj: capacity notes? rough sizing for sustained 100 qps at 512 tokens?

miriam: rough ballpark (sustained, with batching + KV cache warm):
- h100 int8: ~6 GPUs in a single-pop to hit 100 qps with p95 target <200ms
- a100 int8: ~10 GPUs for similar p95 (more due to kernel/warm behavior)
- fp16 variants need ~1.8x the GPUs of int8 (so h100-fp16 ~11 GPUs)

anika: interesting. any kernel flags we should expose in deploy?

miriam: propose exposing preferred_kernel: [fused_attention_v2, fused_attention_v1, generic_nhwc] and an aggressive_warmup boolean that preloads KV caches for hot routes. Aggressive warmup reduces p95 by ~15-25% on repeat traffic in our tests.

deploy-bot: Canary routing policy pushed to eu-west for 30m testing — canary id cny-2026-03-20-001

kevin: next steps?

miriam: 1) run a 12h stability sweep with prefer:local_pop vs prefer:us-east in eu-west/us-west to capture long-tail; 2) add eval gating for top-200 failing prompts under int8; 3) prototype exposing preferred_kernel flag in rollout UI; 4) update capacity calculator with these per-pop multipliers.

raj: +1 on capacity calc update. I'll slot a quick PR to add h100/a100 int8 multipliers to the console estimator.

miriam: thanks — uploading small charts to thread and will open a follow-up with the 12h run results tomorrow. :thumbsup:
